Let $J_u(s,v)$ denote reference-averaged IoU for query target $u$, with $s\in\{0,1\}$ selecting a single concept or full search and $v\in\{0,1\}$ indicating visual boxes.
This measures how much search changes the marginal benefit of visual prompting.
The observed interaction is $-2.85$ percentage points on COCO (95\% CI $[-4.29,-1.48]$) and $-3.00$ on LVIS ($[-4.09,-1.95]$).
Thus, on the full matched input cohort, the two additions have diminishing joint gains: visual boxes help at both search levels, but help more when only the initial concept is used.
